items.name: Mr. Ortiz
items.text: The school caretaker. He knows every switch and wire in the building.

keywords.reply: The storm blew leaves all over the roof. Dirty panels make less power, so the battery doesn't fill up.
The battery is in the small room behind the gym. It has a code lock. The code is hidden in the last line of the meter log, if you can do the math.
Twelve lamps on the path, twenty-five watts each. They should shine from five until ten.
The basketball team practices until five. After that, the gym should be empty.
Those old projectors? Teachers forget to switch them off all the time.
Tuesday night's storm was the biggest one this year.

items.miss: Hmm, I don't know about that. Ask me about the panels, the battery or the gym.

items.name: Lena
items.text: Leader of the school Energy Club. She loves numbers and clean energy.
items.scene: a cheerful student girl with a green Energy Club badge holding a notebook

keywords.reply: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity. It's clean energy: no smoke and no fuel to buy.
The battery saves the day's sunshine for the night. If something uses it up, the lamps go dark.
SDG 7 is Affordable and Clean Energy. Saving energy is part of it too!
The cheapest energy is the energy you don't waste. Switch off what you don't use.
The Winter Fair is on Friday night. Families walk to the bus stop on that path.

items.miss: I'm not sure. Try asking about solar power, the battery or saving energy.

pages.text: Every evening, the solar lamps along the school path light the way to the bus stop. But this week, they go dark before six o'clock.

pages.speaker: Lena
pages.label: Energy Club
pages.text: The lamps run on a battery that the roof panels charge all day. If the battery is empty by six, something is wrong. Will you help me find out what?

pages.title: Your mission
pages.text: Find out why the solar lamps go dark early, and help the school fix it before the Winter Fair on Friday night.

pages.speaker: Mr. Ortiz
pages.label: Caretaker
pages.text: I took this photo on Wednesday morning. Those panels haven't been cleaned since the storm. Ask me anything you like.

pages.title: Puzzle 1: Read the log
pages.text: Look at the Energy Meter Log in your bag. On which day did the solar power suddenly drop?
hints: Compare each day with the day before it.
The storm was on Tuesday night. What happened the next day?
pages.right: Right! After the storm, the panels made less than half the power.
pages.wrong: Not quite. Look for the biggest change from one day to the next.

pages.title: Find the clues
pages.text: Lena opens her notebook. "Two things could drain the battery: weak panels, or something wasting power at night." What will you check?

options.label: Clean the solar panels on the roof

pages.text: You climb up with Mr. Ortiz and wash away the leaves and mud. The panels shine in the sun again. Mr. Ortiz smiles: "Now they can fill the battery."
At 7 p.m. the gym is empty, but the ceiling lights and three old projectors are still on. They all use the same battery as the path lamps!
The battery room. A small screen on the door asks for a code.

ENERGY METER LOG: Harbor Hill School
Solar power made by the roof panels (kWh):
Monday 9.5 | Tuesday 9.1 | Wednesday 4.2 | Thursday 4.0 | Friday 3.8
Note: Big storm on Tuesday night.
NEW: Panels cleaned. Gym lights and projectors were left on at night.
Night lamps: 12 lamps, 25 watts each.

pages.title: Puzzle 2: The battery code
pages.text: The screen says: ENTER THE NIGHT LOAD IN WATTS. Look at the last line of the Energy Meter Log.
hints: The log says: 12 lamps, 25 watts each.
pages.reveal: 12 lamps × 25 watts = 300 watts. The door clicks open.
pages.right: Correct! The screen turns green and the door clicks open.
pages.wrong: The screen beeps. Check the numbers in the log again.

pages.speaker: Lena
pages.label: Energy Club
pages.text: The battery is full again! But the gym will drain it every night unless we change something.

pages.title: Before the Winter Fair
pages.text: The Winter Fair is on Friday. How will you keep the lamps on?

options.label: Put up 'Switch Off' signs and set a timer for the gym lights
Buy a bigger battery and change nothing else

pages.text: The Energy Club puts 'Switch Off' signs in every classroom. Mr. Ortiz sets a timer, so the gym lights and projectors turn off at 6 p.m. Now the battery saves its power for the path.

pages.title: A Bright Winter Fair
pages.text: On Friday night, every solar lamp shines until ten. Families walk safely to the bus stop. You did not need more energy. You just stopped wasting it. That is SDG 7 in action!
You ask the school to buy a bigger battery. It costs a lot of money, and it will take three weeks to arrive. On Friday, the gym lights are still on all night.

pages.title: Still in the Dark
pages.text: The new battery fills up, but the gym empties it again every night. The path stays dark during the fair. A bigger battery cannot fix waste. Try another way!
